intro: You are now at the Great Mosque of Diyarbakır, a mosque and complex in Diyarbakır province, rebuilt in 1091. It is one of Anatolia's oldest mosques. Look at its two-storey courtyard front: its columns and capitals were lifted straight out of the city's Roman buildings.
history: This ground has been sacred for a long time. A Roman temple stood here, and then the church of Mar Toma; when the city was taken in 639, part of the church became a mosque. The building's present form comes from the rebuilding ordered in 1091 by the Seljuk sultan Melikşah. Its two-storey courtyard front was assembled from columns and capitals lifted out of the city's Roman buildings.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the courtyard and its reused Roman columns, the Mesudiye Madrasa and the Zinciriye Madrasa, and, not to be overlooked, the sundial.
facts: Did you know? The sundial in the courtyard is associated with al-Jazari, the engineer and inventor who served the Artuqid court in the twelfth century. The columns and capitals of the courtyard front were taken from the city's Roman buildings and given a second life here. And the mosque forms a complex with the Mesudiye and Zinciriye madrasas, which share its courtyard.
outro: This brings our journey through the Great Mosque of Diyarbakır to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have served many faiths and many centuries; let them keep serving those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
